title: Follow a Tiny Tutorial: Make a Meetup Marker
outcome: Make a marker so your buddy can find your meeting spot. Follow the tiny example, then change its shape, place, or path.
testedVersions: UNVERIFIED - no exact version or input variant has been playtested for revision 2.
multiplayerRequirements: Private local learner world with guardian-visible screen-share, or an adult-owned private Realm. Solo-guided play does not require a second Minecraft account.
knownIncompatibilities: The initial capture recipe targets Bedrock Windows keyboard/mouse only; it is not captured or verified yet.
Touch and controller need their own verified controls and visual assets. Use a preflighted one-action live demo, not mismatched screenshots.
Java imagery and commands are not interchangeable with this Bedrock recipe.

guardianSteps: Sign in and confirm the approved call and learner world work before the session.
Keep the previous build saved; the screenshot studio is a separate adult-only world.
mentorPreflight: Read the exact six-action demo recipe: content/tutorials/bedrock/meetup-marker.json.
Confirm placement and hotbar controls on the learner input method before the session. Do not claim the draft screenshots are ready.
Keep two familiar materials available, plus a learner-selected alternative. A bright decorative cap is optional.
Locate the previous build and two safe nearby marker sites. Keep the learner world in creative mode; do not run studio reset commands there.
The core flow is 35 minutes; use the remaining time for recovery or play. At 30 minutes, stop after a meaningful result and preserve the next idea.

mentorMoves: Ask what they made last time and which place they want a buddy to find.
flow.childAction: Shows or points to a previous creation.

mentorMoves: Offer a marker outside their base or beside a meeting place; accept another safe location.
Help select one familiar block only if needed.
flow.childAction: Places the first block at their chosen spot.

mentorMoves: Show only the next action for 10-30 seconds, then stop. Use the six meetup-marker steps; no unapproved video.
flow.childAction: Watches one action, not the complete build.

mentorMoves: Alternate a single picture or tiny demo with the learner trying it.
flow.childAction: Selects a block, places it, stacks another, switches material, caps the marker, and looks back.

mentorMoves: Ask where you should stand to test whether the marker is easy to find.
In solo-guided play, ask the learner to show the marker from a different nearby spot.
flow.childAction: Tests whether their marker helps locate the meeting place.

mentorMoves: Offer a taller silhouette, a different location, or a short path pointing toward the destination.
Build only a supporting part the learner assigns. Do not correct aesthetic differences.
flow.childAction: Changes the marker so it works for their chosen place.

mentorMoves: Let them show their favourite detail; capture a screenshot only with the required consent.
flow.childAction: Shows or points to the result; spoken explanation is optional.

mentorMoves: Record what they want to make nearby next, the chosen location, and one useful support note. Keep logging under three minutes.
flow.childAction: Chooses a next idea or asks to continue this project.

openingLines: Where should we meet in your world?
Let us make a marker so I can find the place you pick.
keyPhrases: Look at this one action, then you try.
Can I find it from here?
Would you change the shape, the place, or the way to it?

learnerCues.cueText: Place one block on the ground.
Place the glowing block on top.

sharedRoles.childRole: Maker and location chooser - owns the marker and every interesting placement
sharedRoles.mentorRole: Visitor and helper - models one action in a separate demo area, then follows the learner directions
sharedRoles.rotationNotes: The reference slice is one-to-one. Group rotation is not a requirement.

childChoicePoints.prompt: Where should your buddy meet you?
options: At another safe place I choose

childChoicePoints.prompt: What would make your marker easier to find?
options: Add a short path toward it

commonProblems.problem: A block lands beside the stack.
commonProblems.fix: Point at the intended top face. Let the learner remove only that block or keep the new shape if intentional.
Point to the highlighted hotbar slot; let the learner switch. Do not refill their whole inventory.

commonProblems.problem: The learner loses the meeting spot.
commonProblems.fix: Walk back from the previous build together. Keep the marker and add a landmark or path instead of deleting progress.

commonProblems.problem: The picture does not match the device.
commonProblems.fix: Stop using that picture. Use a verified device-specific micro-demo, or one familiar block with spoken/pointed guidance.

hintLadder: What are you trying to make or change?
Point to the matching block or highlighted hotbar slot.
Give one concrete cue: the top face, or the next slot.
Demonstrate that one action in a separate demo area.
With permission, resolve only the blocking mechanical issue; the learner places the meaningful block.
resetPath: Learner recovery is local: undo the last accidental placement, reselect the slot, or walk back together. Preserve all earlier work. Adult world-backup restore is a last resort after saving the current world and explaining what would be lost. The capture compiler resets ONLY a separate disposable studio world.
soloFallback: Learner builds in their own private world while the mentor models one action at a time through approved screen-share. Without usable visual media, use the same concrete three-block example in the mentor demo area. Never demonstrate the entire build while the learner waits.
accessibilityOptions: One instruction per view; mentor reads it when helpful.
No required typing, naming, reflection, or spoken explanation.
Use a one-block marker as a complete small win; expand only when the learner wants.
Offer a stable camera position and short breaks. Verify controls for the actual input method.
safetyRequirements: Private world or adult-owned Realm, guardian-visible communication, no private mentor-child messages.
No account sharing or arbitrary downloads. Adults own setup and administration.
Studio commands must never be executed in learner worlds or shared sessions.
Capture no personal names, chat, account details, or session recordings by default.
parentSummaryTemplate: Today {child} made a meeting marker at {location} and changed {remixDetail}. Next time they want to {nextIdea}.

review.notes: Revision 2 is an authored reference, not a tested lesson. Exact Bedrock version, client settings, screenshots, per-input verification, and a mentor-child playtest remain required.

worldSpecification.description: Continue the learner saved world near a place they care about. Keep two safe marker sites accessible. Exact coordinates, camera poses, and destructive resets in the capture recipe apply only to BB Studio, never to the learner build.
